property_summary: Calling Put with any unlockTime does not change Acc[msg.sender].balance when msg.value == 0 (balance remains equal before and after).
Calling Put with zero wei must not revert (i.e., Put(...) succeeds when value==0).

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after Put completes the contract's stored unlockTime for that caller is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., cannot be in the past); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can store an unlockTime < block.timestamp and thus violate this.

For any caller and any Put call (with any msg.value and _unlockTime), the reference contract guarantees that after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (it never stores a past unlock time); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can store a past time (< block.timestamp) and thus violate this.

For any caller, if Put is called with _unlockTime >= block.timestamp then after Put returns the stored unlockTime for that caller equals that provided _unlockTime (the reference clamps smaller values up to now, so for inputs where _unlockTime >= block.timestamp the stored value must equal _unlockTime); the mutant that unconditionally assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime breaks this when given a future _unlockTime by still storing that value (but the reference also stores it) — instead we target: when Put is called with _unlockTime < block.timestamp the reference stores block.timestamp (i.e. stored unlockTime >= _unlockTime and specifically >= block.timestamp), while the mutant can store a value < block.timestamp, so we restrict fuzzing to ensure _unlockTime may be < block.timestamp and assert that stored unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put.

For any caller and any Put call, after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never less than the current block.timestamp (the reference clamps _unlockTime up to now); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can store a past timestamp (< block.timestamp) and thus violate this.

After any Put call by a caller, the reference contract always ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime is at least the block.timestamp at time of Put (it clamps future values down to now when _unlockTime is in the past); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can store a past timestamp (< block.timestamp) and thus violate this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put increases (or leaves unchanged) that caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value (so balance_after >= balance_before); the mutant subtracts msg.value and can make balance_after < balance_before (indeed decrease), so this property is violated for some inputs.

After any call to Put by an actor with some msg.value, the recorded Acc[actor].balance is never decreased (balance_after >= balance_before); the mutant that does acc.balance -= msg.value can make balance_after < balance_before for some inputs.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put never makes the caller's recorded Acc balance go below zero relative to its previous stored balance (i.e., balance_after >= 0 and specifically balance_after >= balance_before - this holds in reference but the mutant that does acc.balance -= msg.value can make balance_after < balance_before and even underflow in unchecked contexts), so the property asserts balance_after >= balance_before for all inputs and the mutant violates it for some inputs.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put increases the stored Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., balance_after == balance_before + msg.value); the mutant that subtracts msg.value will make balance_after != balance_before + msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and any sent value, executing Put should never decrease the stored Acc[msg.sender].balance (i.e., balance_after >= balance_before); the mutant that subtracts msg.value from acc.balance can make balance_after < balance_before for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, calling Put(...) on the correct contract always increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly msg.value and emits (so balance changes), whereas the mutant early-returns on msg.value==0 causing no state change only for zero-value calls — the universal rule is: if msg.value > 0 then Acc[caller].balance increases by msg.value (the mutant still satisfies this), but importantly the mutant breaks the general rule that a zero-value call to Put still updates unlockTime and logs (i.e., correct contract may update state/log even when msg.value==0) — thus the distinguishing rule is: calling Put with msg.value == 0 preserves that the contract records the call by updating unlockTime and leaving balance unchanged (but observable via LastMsg or unlockTime), which the mutant breaks by returning early.

For any caller and any unlockTime, calling Put with msg.value == 0 still records an entry (updates Log.LastMsg and sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least the call timestamp) in the reference C, whereas the mutant early-returns on zero value and thus does not update logs or unlockTime for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, a zero-ether call to Put should still record the call by updating Acc[caller].unlockTime (and Log.LastMsg), but the mutant that returns early on msg.value==0 fails to update that state for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, calling Put with msg.value == 0 still updates Acc[caller].unlockTime (to at least the current block timestamp) and records a log entry in the reference contract, but the mutant that early-returns on msg.value == 0 fails to update unlockTime (and log) for some inputs, so asserting that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after a zero-value Put distinguishes them.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, a zero-ether call to Put still updates the caller's Acc.unlockTime (to at least the current block timestamp) and records a log entry in the reference contract; the mutant that returns early on msg.value==0 fails to update unlockTime (and thus the log) for some inputs.

For every call to Put by any sender with any value and unlockTime, the reference contract records the operation string "Put" in LogFile.History (the last message Data equals "Put"), whereas the mutant records "Deposit" for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

If Collect transfers out funds (reduces contract balance), then it must also log that transfer by increasing Log.History length (i.e., a successful outgoing ETH transfer is accompanied by a Log.AddMessage call).

property_summary: If Collect call does not revert then either the contract's balance decreased by the withdrawn amount and a log entry was added, or the call reverted; successful non-reverting Collect cannot silently fail to transfer while also not producing a log entry.
If calling Collect does not revert, then the contract's balance must decrease by at least the requested amount (_am).
If Collect does not revert, then the contract balance must decrease by at least the requested amount (_am).

For any caller and amount where the holder has sufficient balance and is unlocked, the reference contract always reverts the Collect call on a failing recipient send (so the holder's recorded balance does not decrease when the external transfer fails), whereas the mutant using send swallows failures and leaves the holder balance decreased even though funds were not transferred.

For any caller, amount and unlock time, if Collect succeeds (does not revert) then the contract's recorded balance for that caller decreases by the same amount as the Ether actually sent out; the mutant that uses send can leave the recorded balance decreased even when the external transfer fails (because send returns false and is not reverted).

For any caller, amount and unlock time where the holder has >= MinSum and is unlocked, the reference implementation always reverts the Collect call if the external transfer to the recipient fails (so the holder's recorded balance is not decreased), whereas the mutant using send does not revert on transfer failure and can leave the holder's recorded balance decreased — i.e. reference: failed external transfer => Collect reverts; mutant: may not revert.

For every Collect(amount) call where the holder has sufficient balance (>=MinSum and >=amount) and is unlocked, if the external transfer to msg.sender fails then the reference contract reverts (so holder balance remains unchanged) while the mutant using send may not revert and can decrease the stored balance despite failing to deliver funds.

For any caller, amount and unlockTime where the caller previously funded the contract (so their stored balance >= MinSum and >= amount) and the recipient's fallback reverts, the reference contract's Collect call always reverts (so the stored balance does not decrease), whereas the mutant that uses send may not revert and can decrease the stored balance despite the external transfer failing.
After a successful Collect call the caller's recorded balance in c (Acc) is decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount immediately (no reentrancy can observe the old balance).

property_summary: A call to Collect(...) never reverts when the caller already has at least MinSum and at least the requested amount and the unlockTime has passed and the contract has sufficient ETH to pay the amount.
If the caller has sufficient recorded balance and unlockTime passed, then Collect must not revert when invoked alone (no reentrancy), i.e. a direct Collect call should succeed for those parameters.
When this test contract calls c.Collect(am) it must not revert (i.e. reverted == false).
When this test contract calls c.Collect(am) (as the caller), the call must not revert.

Invariant: after a successful Collect(amount) call the contract's recorded balance for the caller decreases by exactly amount (acc.balance_post = acc.balance_pre - amount); the mutant that calls the external transfer before decrement allows a reentrant attacker to drain more than allowed, violating this invariant for some inputs.
